source.title: Cascade: Hierarchical Recoverability Control for Large Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Qing-Chen Yu; Shi-Ying Duan; Xiao-Dong Li; Yu-Hua Wang; Zhi-Yu Li; Shi-Ji Zhou; Yi-Fan Sun; Zhaoxin Fan

record.file_problem: The main paper and most appendices are present, but Appendix F.2 ends partway through its final example.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests unlearning and recovery with a new hierarchical method and evaluates recovery under reformulated prompts; it is a conceptual test rather than a reproduction of the original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports post-unlearning target-recovery and utility measures, prompt-reformulation and extraction results, WMDP accuracy, and hidden-state probe results. Reported text says some values are aggregates over prompt categories; Table 8 provides aggregate and extraction metrics, not separate numerical results for each prompt category. No low-bit quantization or small-set recovery fine-tuning attack is run. The hidden-state probes do not establish whether knowledge persists but is inaccessible rather than being removed.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a new unlearning method (Cascade) and measures target recovery after unlearning on TOFU, MUSE-News and WMDP-Cyber, with general-ability checks. It also runs a five-category prompt-reformulation and extraction suite on Cascade and four existing methods. These results bear on A (does unlearning work), F (a counter-method resisting prompt attacks) and, for the baseline methods, E (recovery by prompting). B, C and D are not tested: there is no relearning fine-tuning, no direction ablation and no quantization.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that lowering target-answer likelihood alone may leave knowledge internally recoverable, and that Cascade's path, representation and decoding controls reduce recoverability while keeping utility. They limit the prompt-robustness conclusion to the fixed prompt suite, and treat probes as complementary evidence, not proof of deletion.
record.recipe_differences: Cascade combines selective activation-route suppression, hyperbolic representation compression, and a decoding-level loss; it is not a reproduction of gradient ascent, Who’s Harry Potter, RMU, or the cited original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that retain weight α changes the forgetting–utility trade-off, decoding weight has a stronger effect than path weight, and route-budget performance is relatively stable once routing is enabled. These sensitivity results are primarily figure-described.

fits_no_version.finding: Hidden-state probes recover few targets even from the Original model (Top-1 0.057, Top-5 0.236). Cascade lowers these only slightly (0.042/0.174) while raising the decode NLL gap to 2.47.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lightweight route-module probes are too weak on TOFU to show whether unlearning removes or merely hides knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (venue as stated)
record.problems: The prompt-robustness table does not name its model checkpoint. Prompt recovery is evaluated on the fixed TOFU Forget10 suite, not across the full range of attacks in the claim. Chance-level comparisons are not stated for the main recovery metrics. Main tables generally provide no uncertainty estimates. Hidden-state probes are expressly treated as dependent on their recovery assumptions rather than proof of deletion.
record.rows_left_out: The 59-row selection omits other baseline-method results in Table 1, Table 6 and Table 7; most additional TOFU split/backbone results in Tables 10–22; component ablations in Table 2; and projection, separability, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results in Tables 23–25 and Figures 8–10. These were omitted to prioritize Cascade and reference outcomes, prompt-recovery results across all methods, and direct WMDP results within the row limit.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning, activation-edit or quantization attacks; prompt attacks only on TOFU Forget10.
No direction ablation. Hidden-state probes are too weak to tell blocking from deletion (Original Top-1 is only 0.057).
No jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information. No numeric per-category direct-vs-reformulated comparison per method.
Resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits and quantization is not tested; only the fixed TOFU prompt suite.

missing.what: Targeted-IDK-SFT refusal baseline: Forget ROUGE 0.034 but forget probability 0.79 and extraction strength 0.71. Output-level refusal leaves knowledge extractable, which bears on A for suppression-style methods.
Per-category ASR (Original, Paraphrase, Indirect, Clue, Extraction) per method, needed to see whether reformulation recovers beyond the direct prompt.
Qualitative case: Cascade reproduces target name Tae-ho Park under the strongest extraction prompt (authors call it a rare boundary case).
Table 26 probe values for NPO and RMU (decode gap 0.8174/0.9984; Top-1 0.0576/0.0470; Top-5 0.2472/0.2076).

record.verdict_notes: Table 8 and Table 26 are column-scrambled in the text, and the reader misassigned several values. The main text confirms Cascade Avg ASR 0.10% and extraction ASR 0.25%. In Table 26 the first numeric list after Original is the decode NLL gap, so Original probe Top-1 is about 0.057, not 0.817. Cascade is much weaker on some backbones declared in rows_left_out: Gemma-3-4B Forget10 has forget probability 0.51 and extraction strength 0.74; Qwen3-1.7B Forget01 has forget probability 0.58 and extraction strength 0.71 (Tables 14, 12, 22). Rows for these would add limits_scope for A and F. The Table 8 model checkpoint is unnamed. No uncertainty is reported in the main tables. The study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: No chance-level reference is stated for the reported target metrics; does not test every existing unlearning method or establish that reduced recovery means knowledge was removed.
No post-unlearning recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation; the reported state probes do not distinguish knowledge that is inaccessible from knowledge that has been removed.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests the stated TOFU prompt-reformulation categories, including extraction; does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Cascade is evaluated against the reported prompt-reformulation and extraction suite only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, and quantization is not tested.

tranche.reason: A new method (Cascade) aimed at residual recoverability, plus a fixed reformulation/extraction prompt suite run on Cascade and four existing methods.

source_check.notes: Table 8 columns are scrambled in the text. Using the section 4.2 prose, 5.38/0.35/0.00/0.62/0.10 is Avg ASR and 9.42/1.00/0.00/1.50/0.25 is Extraction ASR.
